title: Dynamic-block adapter capture bounds fast slice
mode: Local adapter implementation with generated focused validation
head: de27a3391a624aba03ca71f3583c4b3a6e6396a9
scope: Bound adapter-owned deep copies of typed dynamic-block callbacks.
Account for the complete current DRW_DynamicBlockObject dynamic payload shape.
Verify successful capture, aggregate budget refusal, and fail-closed export when no callback was retained.

changes.implementation: dx_iface estimates common table-entry/XDATA content, record and scalar strings, flat vectors, nested vectors, fixed-array-of-vector payloads, and vector<bool> logical slots before copying. Capture admits at most 100,000 objects and DRW::kMaxDxfBinaryPayloadBytes logical retained bytes. Refusal or allocation failure sets a sticky dx_data flag; fileExport checks it before writing. The existing dynamic-block no-serializer gate remains unchanged.
changes.limits: Logical payload and container slots are estimated; allocator capacity, implementation-specific list-node overhead, and process RSS are not measured. The adapter aggregate budget is distinct from parser-side limits.
changes.generatedTest: The focused selector constructs a dynamic-block object with scalar strings, string/primitive vectors, nested state/lookup/index vectors, and table-entry XDATA. It verifies successful retention, rejects a second callback after the aggregate budget is saturated, then verifies that a separate empty capture with an over-budget first callback cannot publish output. No drawing fixture is used.

nonClaims: This bounds adapter-side logical copies, not allocator capacity or process RSS.
No dynamic-block graph semantics or DXF serializer support claim is established.
J256, J260, J268, J284, J293, and J295 remain DEFERRED_EXTERNAL and non-promoting.
No external drawings or repository fixtures were added.
The shared worktree is extensively dirty; no staging or commit occurred.
